Document: Practice Direction 54A – Judicial review
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
An electronic version of the bundle shall be prepared in accordance with the Guidance on the Administrative Court website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > The hearing bundle and the authorities bundle] 16.5 Not less than 7 days before the date of the hearing (or the warned date), the parties shall lodge the authorities bundle with the Court in both electronic and hard copy form. For Divisional Court cases the number of hard copy bundles required will be one set for each judge hearing the case. ## Agreed final order

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > Agreed final order] 17.1 If, prior to judgment being given on a claim the parties agree the terms of a final order to be made disposing of the claim, the claimant shall file 3 copies of the proposed agreed order together with a short, agreed statement of the matters relied on as justifying the proposed agreed order and copies of any authorities or statutory provisions relied on. Both the draft order and the agreed statement shall be signed by all parties to the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > Agreed final order] 17.2 The court will consider the documents referred to in paragraph 17.1 and will make the order if satisfied that the order should be made. ## 17.3 If the court is not satisfied that the order should be made, a hearing date will be set. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 17.3 If the court is not satisfied that the order should be made, a hearing date will be set.] 17.4 Where the agreement relates to an order for costs only, the parties need only file a document signed by all the parties setting out the terms of the proposed order. ## 18.1 (1) This section applies where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (a) a person has been served with a copy of directions for his removal from the United Kingdom by UK Visas and Immigration (“UKVI”) and notified that this section applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (b) that person makes an application for permission to apply for judicial review before his removal takes effect. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (2) This section does not prevent a person from applying for judicial review after he has been removed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.2 (1) A person who makes an application for permission to apply for judicial review must file a claim form and a copy at court, and the Claim Form must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (a) indicate on its face that this Section of the Practice Direction applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (b) be accompanied by—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (i) a copy of the removal directions and the decision to which the application relates; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (ii) any document served with the removal directions including any document which contains the UKVI’s factual summary of the case; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (c) contain or be accompanied by a clear and concise statement of the claimant’s grounds for bringing the claim for judicial review; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (d) state the claimant’s Home Office reference number;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] If the claimant is unable to comply with paragraph (b) or (c) or (d) above the Claim Form must contain or be accompanied by a statement of the reasons why. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (2) The claimant must, immediately upon issue of the claim, send copies of the issued Claim Form and accompanying documents to the address specified by the UKVI . [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] ( Rule 54.7 (opens in a new tab) also requires the defendant to be served with the Claim Form within 7 days of the date of issue. Rule 6.10 (opens in a new tab) provides that service on a Government Department must be effected on the solicitor acting for that Department, which in the case of the UKVI is the Government Legal Department (“GLD”). The address for GLD may be found in the Annex to Part 66 of these Rules (opens in a new tab) .)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.3 Where the claimant has not complied with paragraph 18.2(1)(b) or (c) or (d) but has provided reasons why he is unable to comply, and the court has issued the Claim Form, the Administrative Court—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (a) will refer the matter to a Judge for consideration as soon as practicable; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] (b) will notify the parties that it has done so. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 18.4 If, upon a refusal to grant permission to apply for judicial review, the Court decides that the application is clearly without merit, that decision will be included in the order refusing permission. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] 19.1 A person who makes an application for permission to apply for judicial review of the decision of the Upper Tribunal refusing permission to appeal must file a Claim Form which must: (a) state on its face that the application is made under Rule 54.7A (opens in a new tab) ; (b) identify which of the categories at Rule 54.7A(1)(a) – (c) apply; and (c) set out succinctly the grounds relied on in support of the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 54A – JUDICIAL REVIEW > 18.1 (1) This section applies where—] Updated: Saturday, 6 April 2024
